policy: Wildcard IAM actions are forbidden. Resource or principal wildcards are accepted only when AWS requires them or when an explicit Deny cannot grant access. Every occurrence is counted and tied to a statement context.

exceptions.reason: CloudWatch log streams have AWS-generated names, so the shared API Gateway logging role must target all streams beneath only the two explicitly named health-check log groups.
logs:DescribeLogGroups does not support resource-level authorization; aws:RequestedRegion limits discovery to the configured Region.
KMS key IDs are generated by AWS. Deployment policy statements using this template add project and environment tag conditions and the key policy provides a second authorization boundary.
Lambda creates log stream names dynamically; the ARN remains constrained to the exact environment-prefixed Lambda log group.
API Gateway creates log streams dynamically; the ARN remains constrained to the exact environment-prefixed API access log group.
REST API child resource identifiers are generated by API Gateway. The deployment role is limited to the regional REST API resource family needed by this stack.
API key IDs are generated by API Gateway; the permission remains limited to the API key resource family in the configured Region.
Usage plan IDs are generated by API Gateway; the permission remains limited to the usage-plan resource family in the configured Region.
API Gateway tag resources contain generated API identifiers, so Terraform needs the regional tag resource family to maintain environment-tagged API resources.
VPC IDs are generated by EC2; subsequent mutations are additionally restricted by Project and Environment resource-tag conditions.
Subnet IDs are generated by EC2; subsequent mutations are additionally restricted by Project and Environment resource-tag conditions.
Route table IDs are generated by EC2; subsequent mutations are additionally restricted by Project and Environment resource-tag conditions.
Security group IDs are generated by EC2; subsequent mutations are additionally restricted by Project and Environment resource-tag conditions.
VPC endpoint IDs are generated by EC2; subsequent mutations are additionally restricted by Project and Environment resource-tag conditions.
A KMS key policy uses Resource star to mean the key to which the policy is attached; the principal and every allowed KMS action are explicitly enumerated.
The wildcard type and identifier apply only to an explicit Deny for insecure transport, so they cannot grant S3 access to any principal.
The Deny must cover every object in the exact Terraform state bucket to prevent plaintext transport of state objects.
The wildcard type and identifier apply only to an explicit Deny for TLS versions below 1.2 and therefore cannot grant S3 access.
The TLS Deny must cover every object under the exact Terraform state bucket.
The wildcard type and identifier occur only in an explicit Deny that enforces KMS object encryption and cannot grant S3 access.
The encryption Deny must cover every object in the exact Terraform state bucket.
The wildcard type and identifier occur only in an explicit Deny enforcing the exact state KMS key and cannot grant S3 access.
The key-enforcement Deny must cover every object in the exact Terraform state bucket.
kms:CreateKey cannot target an ARN for a key that does not exist yet; key spec, usage, multi-Region state, project tag, and environment tag are constrained.
kms:ListAliases is a list operation without resource-level authorization; no KMS mutation is included in this statement.
The required EC2 Describe APIs do not support resource-level authorization; aws:RequestedRegion prevents cross-Region discovery.
EC2 resource IDs do not exist before create operations; mandatory Project and Environment request tags constrain creation and later mutations use resource-tag conditions.
logs:DescribeLogGroups does not support resource-level authorization; aws:RequestedRegion limits discovery to the configured Region.
Lambda VPC ENI lifecycle APIs cannot be scoped to network-interface ARNs that do not exist yet; only the exact mandatory EC2 actions are allowed.
This explicit Deny applies the same unavoidable ENI resource scope to block function-code ENI calls identified by lambda:SourceFunctionArn.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; the break-glass principal and administration actions are explicit.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; the environment deployment-role principal and administration actions are explicit.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; CallerAccount and ViaService constrain cryptographic use to DynamoDB in this account and Region.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; CreateGrant is limited to AWS-resource grants made through DynamoDB for this account and Region.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; the exact runtime role is constrained to DynamoDB plus the exact table encryption context.
KMS key policies use Resource star for the attached key; CreateGrant is restricted to AWS-resource grants through DynamoDB for the exact runtime role.
DynamoDB VPC endpoint policies use Principal star, while aws:PrincipalArn narrows effective access to the exact Lambda runtime role and the statement allows only PutItem to the exact table.
